subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@aureliahealth.com>, Jenny Li <jenny.li@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call / next steps

Hi Sam / Jenny —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and appreciated the context on your internal timelines. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Primary use case: clinical summarization and triage (API-driven flows integrated into EHR workflows).
- Expected traffic profile: a mix of steady daytime usage with short bursts around shift changes.
- Quality & privacy: PHI-sensitive, looking at Private/Dedicated deployment options and KMS integration.

Next steps we agreed on: schedule a dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive) so our infra/serving team can align on throughput, latency SLOs, and any security/network constraints. To help make that call productive, I've attached a small capacity worksheet (aurelia_capacity_template_v1.xlsx) — if you can pre-fill the highlighted cells it will speed the conversation.

Proposed attendees from our side: Logan Wright (inference engineer), Neha Kapoor (solutions), and Vivek Kulkarni (product lead). Please let me know who from your side should join (I expect the infra/engineering lead + product owner).

Suggested time slots (PST):
- Tue Mar 2, 10:00–11:00
- Wed Mar 3, 14:00–15:00
- Thu Mar 4, 09:00–10:00

Also, a few requests for the worksheet / for the call so we can come prepared:
- Peak concurrent requests and average requests per minute
- Typical input sequence length (tokens) and output length (tokens)
- Burst characteristics (how long bursts last, expected concurrency during bursts)
- Any throughput latency targets (p95/p99) and error budget constraints

If you prefer, we can do a shorter sync first and then a deeper sizing call with Logan and our infra team.

Thanks — looking forward to locking a time.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.coole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: aurelia_capacity_template_v1.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@aureliahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenny Li <jenny.li@aureliahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. Appreciate the worksheet, we'll try to fill in what we can ahead of time. A few quick answers based on our initial estimates:

- Expected steady-state: ~8–12 reqs/sec during daytime hours.
- Peak bursts: up to ~60 concurrent requests for 1–3 minute windows during shift changes.
- Avg input tokens: ~150 tokens. Avg output tokens: ~80 tokens.
- Target latency: p95 <= 400ms; p99 <= 800ms for the majority of flows. For lower-priority background jobs, we can tolerate higher latency.

Attendees: Jenny Li (infra lead) and myself for sure; I may also loop in our security lead if necessary.

Of the proposed slots, Thu Mar 4, 09:00–10:00 PST works best for us. If that works for your team, please lock it.

—Sam
Director of Engineering | Aurelia Health
sam.taylor@aureliahealth.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@aureliahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing call / next steps

Thanks Sam — that's super helpful and aligns with what we expected. A couple of quick clarifying questions so we can prepare tests and a preliminary sizing: 

1) Burst profile: when you say "up to ~60 concurrent requests for 1–3 minute windows", is that typically a hard spike (all requests arrive within a 5–10s ramp) or more of a gradual increase over the 1–3 minute window?

2) Variance in sequence length: are those 150/80 token averages consistent across users, or do you have long-tail cases (e.g., 500–1000 tokens) we should account for in worst-case memory sizing?

3) Authentication & routing: will requests originate from a single VPC egress range (we can attach an L4 rule) or multiple egress IPs / regions? Also, any requirements around mutual TLS or custom CA?

Agenda I'm thinking for the call (30–45m):
- Quick intros & success criteria (5m)
- Walk through their traffic profile & worksheet (10m)
- Preliminary capacity/sizing recommendations (15m)
- Next steps & action items (5–10m)

I'll prepare some rough TPS vs latency curves and a few sizing options (1x baseline, 2x buffer, burst-tail config) so we can discuss tradeoffs.

If Thu Mar 4 09:00 PST is confirmed, I'll bring a short slide with those options and a simple test plan.

—Logan
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
